questions.q: What is Terraform Core responsible for?
options: Making direct API calls to every cloud provider
Parsing .tf files, building the dependency graph, and computing plans
Storing cloud provider billing information
Hosting the Terraform Registry
questions.explain: Core handles the provider-independent work — parsing configuration, building the dependency graph, and comparing desired state to real state to compute a plan.

options: A cloud subscription plan
A plugin binary that translates resource blocks into real API calls for one specific service
A type of Terraform state file
The company that maintains Terraform
questions.explain: A provider is a separate plugin, like azurerm or aws, that Terraform Core downloads and talks to in order to actually create resources in a specific cloud.

questions.q: Why can't Terraform Core create an Azure virtual machine by itself, without the azurerm provider?
options: Core has no built-in knowledge of any specific cloud API — that logic lives entirely in provider plugins
Azure virtual machines require a different programming language
Core only works with on-premises infrastructure
Terraform does not support virtual machines at all
questions.explain: Core is provider-agnostic. Every resource type's actual API calls are implemented inside the relevant provider plugin, not in Core itself.

questions.q: What role does state play in Terraform's architecture?
options: It stores a copy of all your .tf source files as a backup
It records every resource Terraform manages along with its real-world ID, so Terraform can detect drift
It is only used during terraform init
It replaces the need for providers
questions.explain: State ties your configuration to real infrastructure by recording each managed resource's real-world ID, letting Terraform know what already exists and compare it against desired configuration.

options: A paid add-on sold by HashiCorp
A community-governed, open-source fork of Terraform with the same core architecture
A replacement for the azurerm provider
A tool unrelated to Terraform that manages only AWS resources
questions.explain: OpenTofu is a fork of Terraform created after a licensing change, maintained by the community, and largely wire-compatible with existing Terraform configuration.
